attempts.systemPrompt:
Trip shape: multi-city
Specialist: route-and-logistics

You are the route and logistics specialist on a trip-planning tool.
You propose the legs this trip is made of — drives, rides, transfers, ferries and trains — with the stops that make a long one bearable.

You propose options. You never write a schedule: nothing you return says which day it falls on, what order things happen in, or what time anything starts. Another part of this tool packs the days, in code.

Rules, and they are not negotiable:
- Reply with JSON and nothing else, in exactly this shape:
{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "title": "short, and never an itinerary",
      "summary": "why this is worth doing, in a sentence or two",
      "location": { "kind": "at", "place": { "name": "...", "locality": "... or null", "coordinates": null } },
      "durationMinutes": 0,
      "cost": { "currency": "ISO-4217", "low": 0, "high": 0, "basis": "per-person | per-party", "provenance": { "kind": "model-asserted" } },
      "season": { "from": "MM-DD", "to": "MM-DD" },
      "bookingLeadTimeDays": 0
    }
  ]
}
- At most 6 candidates. Fewer is a fine answer; an empty list is a fine answer.
- Anything you do not know is null. A duration nobody measured is null, not a plausible ninety minutes. A season nobody checked is null — which is not the same as all year, and all year is written {"from":"01-01","to":"12-31"}.
- Costs are bands with a currency and a basis, never a single figure and never a quote. Do not total anything.
- A slot that says "not answered" is unknown to you. Say in the summary what you could not account for, and propose anyway. Never invent the answer and never refuse to propose.
- Never book anything, never ask for payment details, and never present what you write as clearance to go anywhere.
- Every candidate is a movement, so its location is {"kind":"between","from":{...},"to":{...}} with **both** ends as places. Endpoints in the title are not endpoints, and a candidate that puts them there is discarded.
- This trip has 13 days.
- **Nothing you propose may be longer than 300 minutes.** That is the party's own answer about how much a day holds, translated into minutes. Something longer has to be split into parts that each fit, or not proposed — a candidate over that ceiling is discarded and the plan comes back missing this part of itself.

candidates.title: Railjet, first half of the Vienna–Ljubljana link
candidates.summary: The direct Vienna–Ljubljana train runs about six hours, which is over the day's ceiling, so this splits it at Graz. Graz works as a short stop or an overnight. I could not account for access needs or ages. Check current timetables.

candidates.title: Train across the Austrian–Slovenian border via Maribor
candidates.summary: This is the second half of the Vienna–Ljubljana link, through wine country into Slovenia. I have not measured the duration, so confirm it fits the five-hour day. Access needs are not answered.

candidates.title: Karst crossing by rail to the Adriatic
candidates.summary: This is a short hop from Ljubljana down through the Karst to the coast. The direct cross-border train has run only in some seasons, and I have not checked that it runs in May–June 2027. A change at Sežana or a coach may be needed instead.

candidates.title: Regional train along the Friulian plain
candidates.summary: This is the first part of the Trieste–Vienna link, which is too long to do in one day. Udine is a pleasant place to pause. Fares are flat regional tickets. The duration is unmeasured.

candidates.title: Cross-border train over the Alps into Carinthia
candidates.summary: This is the middle part of the Trieste–Vienna link, a scenic Alpine crossing. It may be a train or the MiCoTra service. I have not checked the service pattern or the duration.

candidates.title: Railjet through the Austrian interior
candidates.summary: This is the last part of the Trieste–Vienna link. I have not measured the duration, and it may be close to the five-hour ceiling, so confirm it before relying on it. If it runs over, split it again at Klagenfurt or Graz. Access needs are not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel near Vienna Hauptbahnhof
candidatesAccepted.summary: A comfortable mid-to-upper hotel near the main station keeps the train links to Ljubljana and Trieste simple and suits a moderate-effort pace. Access needs and any age considerations were not answered, so check step-free rooms and lifts directly.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel in Vienna's inner districts
candidatesAccepted.summary: A comfortable hotel in the Innere Stadt or Neubau puts the main sights within walking distance, so less effort is needed each day. Late spring is busy, so book early. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel in Ljubljana old town
candidatesAccepted.summary: A comfortable hotel in or beside the pedestrian old town is a short walk or taxi from the station. Rooms in the old town are limited, so May–June books up. Access needs were not answered, and cobbles and older buildings may matter.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel near Trieste's Piazza Unità
candidatesAccepted.summary: A comfortable hotel near the seafront and Piazza Unità d'Italia is within easy reach of Trieste Centrale. Access needs were not answered, and parts of the city are hilly.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel near Trieste Centrale
candidatesAccepted.summary: A practical comfortable hotel by the station, a good choice if Trieste is the arrival or departure city by train. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Kunsthistorisches Museum
candidatesAccepted.summary: One of Europe's great art collections (Bruegel, Vermeer, Caravaggio) in a grand Ringstrasse building; a comfortable, moderate-effort half day. Access needs were not answered, so step-free routes are not accounted for here.

candidatesAccepted.title: Schönbrunn Palace and gardens
candidatesAccepted.summary: Habsburg summer palace with state rooms and extensive gardens up to the Gloriette; May–June is a good time for the grounds. Walking distances are considerable; access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Naschmarkt grazing in Vienna
candidatesAccepted.summary: Vienna's long-running open-air market, good for grazing stalls and a sit-down lunch among locals. Dietary restrictions and access needs were not answered, so check stalls on the day.

candidatesAccepted.title: Heuriger wine-tavern evening
candidatesAccepted.summary: A wine tavern on Vienna's edge serving its own young wine with a cold buffet is a distinctly Viennese meal. This is a kind of place, not a specific one. Opening varies by tavern and was not checked; dietary needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Traditional Viennese coffee house
candidatesAccepted.summary: Coffee and cake in a classic coffee house is part of Vienna's culture rather than a snack stop. This is a kind of place; pick one near where you stay. Dietary needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Odprta kuhna street-food market
candidatesAccepted.summary: Ljubljana's open-air food market gathers Slovenian and local restaurant stalls in one square. It runs on certain days in warmer months; exact dates were not checked. Dietary needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Trieste buffet lunch
candidatesAccepted.summary: Trieste's buffets serve boiled pork, sausages and sauerkraut with horseradish, a meal where Austro-Hungarian and Italian food meet. This is a kind of place, not a named one; dietary needs were not answered and this style is meat-heavy.

candidatesAccepted.title: Historic café in Trieste
candidatesAccepted.summary: Trieste is a coffee city; ordering a 'capo in b' at a historic café is a small ritual worth making time for. This is a kind of place. Dietary needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Check and apply for ETIAS travel authorisation
candidatesAccepted.summary: Canadian passport holders are expected to need an ETIAS authorisation for Schengen countries (Austria, Slovenia, Italy) by 2027; confirm it is in force before travel and apply well ahead. Ages were not answered, so I could not account for fee exemptions for younger or older travellers. Check passport validity at the same time. This is not clearance to travel.

candidatesAccepted.title: Travel medical and cancellation insurance
candidatesAccepted.summary: Canadian provincial health plans cover little abroad, so medical, evacuation and trip-cancellation cover is worth arranging for a 12-night multi-country trip. Ages and access needs were not answered, and both can change premiums and what policies cover.

candidatesAccepted.title: Advance rail tickets Vienna–Ljubljana–Trieste
candidatesAccepted.summary: Vienna–Ljubljana has direct trains with cheaper advance fares from ÖBB and Slovenian Railways; Ljubljana–Trieste rail service is thin and may need a change or a coach, so check that leg early in case you prefer dropping a city. Fares are bands, not quotes.

candidatesAccepted.title: EU data eSIM for Austria, Slovenia and Italy
candidatesAccepted.summary: Canadian roaming plans are costly; one EU eSIM covers all three countries under EU roaming rules, useful for train apps and maps. Confirm your phones are unlocked and eSIM-capable.
